Lomza Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Łomża, Poland

Not demolished. Łomża's Jewish community, present from the end of the 15th century, faced settlement restrictions from 1598, when local Jews were expelled to the nearby village of Rybaki; the community revived at the turn of the 19th century, reaching 9,131 people (41 percent of the city) by 1921, most later killed by the Germans in nearby Giełczyn and at Auschwitz-Birkenau. This, the older of Łomża's two Jewish cemeteries, was established in either 1822 or 1833, according to various sources; the authors of the Memorial Book of the Jewish Community in Łomża claimed it stood on the site of an earlier 16th-century cemetery, though this is unconfirmed elsewhere. In 1988, city authorities cleaned the site and established a lapidarium.
